newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-PRICE BACK ON FAVOURITE COURSE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PRICE BACK ON FAVOURITE COURSE.

text.p: Nick Price, runner up to Fiji's Vijay Singh in last week's South African Open, returns to one of his favourite courses on Thursday for the Dimension Data pro-am, an event co-sanctioned by the European Tour.
Zimbabwe's Price is back at the Gary Player Country Club course -- the site of "four of the best rounds I've ever put together in a week."
Two years ago Price shattered Bernhard Langer's course aggregate record by eight shots with an extraordinary 24 under par total of 264.

But unlike the Million Dollar challenge, this event will be split between the Gary Player Country Club and the adjoining Lost City golf course, a spectacular layout with tees blasted into the rock face of the Magaliesberg mountains and notoriously hard and fast greens.

Although Singh and Ernie Els will not be at Sun City, the European link to the tournament has ensured the presence of two past winners at Sun City, former U.S. Masters champions Ian Woosnam and Severiano Ballesteros.

The Welshman would also have been in contention last week had he not posted a disastrous 75 in the second round. But the three other rounds of 66, 69 and 69 left him in joint seventh place and he, like Price, showed excellent early season form, particularly with the driver.

Zimbabwe's Mark McNulty, with three wins in five tournaments on the South African tour and a third place last week, is certain to challenge again, along with last year's South African Order of Merit winner, Wayne Westner.
Three-time Million Dollar Challenge winner David Frost must also be a contender given his affinity with the layout.

But the winner will have to be patient with more than just his game and the course; the professionals are paired with amateurs - who could be anything between scratch and 18 handicap players - for all four days of the event.
